reviews.text:
Cala is the kind of place that reminds you why going out to eat can still feel like an adventure.

In a city packed with polished concepts and interchangeable cocktail menus, Cala manages to have something increasingly rare: personality. The room hums with energy, the food arrives with purpose, and every detail feels intentional without trying too hard.

The real standout of the evening, though, was Sarah behind the bar. Great bartenders do more than pour drinks… they set the tone for the entire experience. Sarah has that effortless combination of knowledge, humor, and hospitality that makes you want to stay for “just one more.” Whether steering you toward the right cocktail or keeping the conversation flowing, she made the night memorable.

The food was vibrant, beautifully executed, and packed with flavor. Nothing felt phoned in. Every plate seemed designed to be shared, discussed, and enjoyed at a pace that encourages lingering.

Cala isn’t just another Scottsdale hotspot. It’s a place where good food, strong drinks, and genuine hospitality come together in a way that feels authentic. And in a world increasingly filled with restaurants chasing trends, authenticity is worth celebrating.

Five stars. I’ll be thinking about this meal, and Sarah’s hospitality, for a long time.

I was very disappointed with my experience at this restaurant. We booked a reservation for 10 people for my bachelorette party and agreed to a minimum spend of $850, which was completely reasonable and something we were prepared to meet.

During the evening, the company I work for surprised our group with three bottles of champagne and a round of shots to celebrate. Unfortunately, instead of working with us, the restaurant informed us that the drinks purchased for us could not be applied toward our minimum spend. As a result, despite our group spending heavily throughout the night, we were left about $200 short of the minimum and essentially had to spend additional money we hadn’t planned on.

While I understand that restaurants have policies, this felt extremely inflexible and left a sour impression on what should have been a special celebration. A little discretion and customer service would have gone a long way. It’s frustrating to be penalized because someone generously purchased drinks for your table.

The food was underwhelming, especially for the price point, and the overall experience felt disorganized and unwelcoming.

第一次來 CALA Scottsdale 慶生，整體用餐體驗相當不錯。

這次點了 Turkish Eggs 和 Brioche French Toast，兩道主餐都很有特色。Turkish Eggs 的優格與半熟蛋搭配得很有層次，而 French Toast 口感濕潤柔軟，甜而不膩

唯一比較可惜的是候位時間比預期久了不少，即使有預約還是等待了一段時間。另外這次剛好是生日來用餐，原本以為會有一些小驚喜或慶生活動，但餐廳並沒有特別安排。

不過整體來說，餐點品質、環境氛圍與現場音樂都很值得體驗。如果喜歡有度假感又適合拍照的早午餐餐廳，CALA 仍然是 Scottsdale 很值得造訪的選擇。

We gladly took them and before we even got the first sip in Eric comes over and says “there’s no drinks in the lobby, you can either go over there or get out.” We apologized and explained that they just handed us the drinks so we didn’t realize to which he responded “I don’t care. You can either go over there or get out.” No one was even trying to argue with him, but he was exceptionally rude for no reason.

Then, the service. We were there with a preselected menu due to the size of the party. There were not any food modifications made on the spot. It took almost 40 min from the time we were first seated until the first appetizer came out. I say the first because the appetizers were not brought out at the same time. The main course was fine. The desert was not the desert we had preordered. We also only got water one time when we first sat down and then never again till we asked almost 2 hours later. By the end of the meal we were just so done and ready to be out of there but it also took long enough for the check to come that people from the group started getting up to try to find our server.

That said, I was disappointed with the service from our server tonight. It took quite a while for him to come by our table, and throughout the evening he rarely checked in to see how the food or experience was going despite the dissipating crowd. Our dessert also took at least 30 minutes to arrive.
Grabbing our receipts, another 5 min. There were 6 of us. We asked if he could put 2 entrees (no drinks) on a separate bill/card and charge the rest to one card to make it easier for our group to split between CAD and USD credit cards. He declined and told us we would need to reconcile the total amongst ourselves.

There were also a few service details that stood out in a negative way — while refilling our water, water was spilled around the table without an apology, and at one point he reached across to grab plates without excusing himself. Overall, the service felt unenthusiastic and lacking some of the basic attentiveness and manners you would expect from a restaurant of this caliber.

reviews.text:
I normally give restaurants grace when going out as a someone who has worked in the service industry for 7 years myself, but this was one of the worst experiences I’ve had at a restaurant.

Before getting seated for our reservation, we had to wait almost 15 minutes because they were behind, we were one of the last reservations for the evening so it was already very late.

Manny our server did not greet us or introduce himself to the table at all. He brought menus, and went straight into asking for our drink order, then proceeded to tell us we needed to hurry and order because the kitchen was closing soon.

Why take reservations that late if you are going to rush patrons into ordering? I personally think that’s a bad way to start off the evening, and a bad look on a restaurant. You feed your seated guests, no matter what the time. We didn’t even get to order dessert, and it was for a special occasion.

We were going out with large group of friends, and I did not pick the restaurant, but I have allergies and am sober, and it is difficult even wanting to go out to restaurants like this because it’s hard finding food to work with my allergies. I proceeded to inform him, I would need things rung up without dairy, and he said “it’s a Mediterranean restaurant, nothing here is dairy free,” with attitude. Which already made me feel like I was a burden to him.

With the first drink order, I asked for a soda and didn’t receive it until after the food had already come out (30 minutes after we had sat down) and I had to ask him about it again. He said, “it’s kind of out of the way to get it, so I just haven’t had time.” Again with attitude.

When it was dropped at the table, it was flat, the ice was melted and it was clear that it had been sitting out before bringing it to the table.

Others on our table enjoyed the food for the most part, however the food runners did not seem to know which items went to which seat number, which is usually a mistake made by the server, which confused them and made it difficult for us.

Once the food was served, we had no check up by Manny asking how it tasted, most of our drinks never received a refill and after the food came out, we rarely saw him again.

Overall, pretty bad experience especially for the price of everything, and atmosphere, it feels like a nice restaurant.

For management,

If you have your server on a large table, you need to train them how to properly take care of a large table and give them a good experience, proper seat numbers, and etiquette when serving high ticket tables. The sad part is, we were auto grated 20% for the large party.

And it was not deserved. Do better next time, properly set up your servers with training for success and your staff to coordinate together and give them resources to improve wait times for other times like soft drinks and sides.

If I were you choosing this restaurant be weary of going out with large group. They are not properly set up and trained to serve large groups.

5 stars and also… what just happened 😂

Cala Scottsdale said “you thought this was JUST dinner?” and then proceeded to turn it into a full production come 9:30 pm.

We walked in and immediately it was a vibe — dim lighting, cocktail dB buzz, indoor/outdoor Scottsdale living. But then, come 9-9:30 pm on a Friday right, there are suddenly sparklers, tables are cheering, our waiter Luca is doing the most. We didn’t hate it; in fact, we fed into it.

Food held its own too. The Peruvian scallop crudo was fresh, flaming saganaki was cheesy literally on fire in the best way, and penne alla vodka was solid comfort. Also shoutout to the honeycrisp and frisée salad for making me feel slightly balanced through all of this chaos and cocktails.

Drinks were IT though. The matcha sour was SO good I had two, and the espresso martini flight was a group favorite. They were full sized cocktails!

If you want quiet and intimate, this is not that. If you want dinner with a plot twist in the coolest part of town… this is absolutely that.

On Opentable we were told we would be charged $25 per person if canceling less than 24 hours in advance or for no shows.    So, we arrived early and we were seated outside.  Then everything went downhill.

A couple who was seated near us was vaping and we were inhaling it.   I went to hostess and she asked me if i want manager to talk to the couple or do i want her to move us to another seat.   We are on vacation and we just wanted to have a nice dinner so I asked her if she can just move us to another seat which was inside.

Now, this is the problem. IF vaping is illegal in outdoor dining areas in Scottsdale, that couple should have been approached way before we arrived there and they were supposed to be asked not to vape there or to leave.  We are not from around here and I don't know what the are laws about vaping in dining areas.

We ordered Margharita pizza, Rigatoni Bolognese and Lamb Shank. Margharita pizza was horrible - that was plain NY style pizza with cheapest cheese there is.   Definitley not good or worth the money.   Rigatoni bolognese was just OK, with huge chunks of meat ( even though that should be ground meat) and lamb shank was good.

When it comes to dress code - there is NONE.   We somehow were led believe this might be an upscale restaurant but it definitely is not.   We saw couple of guys wearing beanie, baseball cap and flip flops, and sleeveless muscle shirts.    Gross.

The last thing - music was so loud that we couldn't hear each other.

This restaurant is nicely decorated and they are trying to be upscale but it's not working.

We wish we would have gone somewhere else but now we know.

We won't come back and we wouldn't recommend this place.

reviews.text:
The food I had tasted inauthentic. The Tamarind Braised Lamb Shank was sweet forward with heat and raw spices that lacked depth. The palatable direction was either sweet or heat, but neither coming to a coherent and desirable space. Although the bone marrow within the lamb shank gave the indication of a slow simmered fall off the bone, the flavors in the sauce were lacking in time and effort. The garbanzo beans seemed canned, undercooked, and flavorless. Sitting in a sauce with another legume and spices that could be distinguished in flavor from one another; due to this lack of slow simmer. It was basic at best and a $46 disappointment. Leading me to compare it to, and making it the lesser option between Costco’s refrigerated aisle Lamb Shank and this one.

Service was less than accommodating from hosts to bar tenders. Although, servers and bussers seemed more in-tuned with providing good service. Very few guests seemed to order from the dinner menu while I was there. Which gave me the indication that this place’s 4.5 stars comes from the social bar atmosphere, rather than fine dining.

Additionally, the space has a confusing and restrictive happy hour seating structure. Where only the seats right at the bar are reserved for happy hour. Therefore guests swarm around the bar, while the rest of the restaurant and seats even two feet from the bar sit empty.

The decor and ambiance here are beautiful—the blend of indoor/outdoor space and lighting creates a great initial vibe. Unfortunately, the service and food quality didn't come close to matching the "upscale" price tag.
​We started with the whipped ricotta ($20). It was delicious, but came with only two pieces of bread. We were shocked to see a $4 surcharge on the bill later for two extra slices of bread needed to actually finish the appetizer. The meatballs were good, but the entrees were a major letdown. My black truffle and sausage pasta was so salty it was difficult to eat, and the Margherita pizza was inedible—soggy, not crispy, and looked like a standard cheese pizza with burnt, bitter basil (see photo).
​Service was non-existent. Our waitress was cold, offered no recommendations, and never checked why we left an entire pizza on the table. My wife actually had to grab clean plates from another table herself. To top it off, they charge a 3% credit card surcharge—which feels nickel-and-dime for a place charging $60 for a $20 bottle of wine. We even had to ask the hostess for a bag for our wine just to stay compliant with state law. Great decor, but they need to learn what "high-end service" actually means.

Cala has potential, maybe with a stretch, but my lunch visit was a masterclass in poor hospitality. Seated at the bar, the service was inattentive for the most part. The food was mediocre at best,  unremarkable for the price.
The real issue: despite showing up, informing the host I was dining solo, and spending over $100 on lunch for one, I later received a no-show email and was charged a $50 no-show fee. Incompetent hosting at minimum, dishonest billing at worst.

What makes it worse,  the charge appeared on my credit card two months later, clearly hoping I wouldn’t catch it. I had to dispute it with my credit card company.

Warning to fellow diners: Monitor your statements well after your visit. Keep your receipts.

Cala won’t be getting a second chance from me.

Now for the uninspiring stuff; very noisy, drinks were slow, very limited wine selection, Wait staff moved around in a rushed manner which made it obvious they were spread thin, but everyone was very pleasant. Our lovely waitress was hurried to get our orders in. Would also mention that La Cala describes itself as an ‘elevated dining experience’ however the inside ambience I would describe as a high energy sports bar with blaring speakers overhead.
Would I come back? Yes, I would come back but would request to do lunch on the outside patio where we could have a normal conversation without the need of raising our voices. I will also be more dressed down and with a lowered expectation. The food quality on our first is worth the second visit.

Both times we were seated in the bar area which has loud music and not the same ambiance as  the restaurant side with open outdoor/indoor seating. There were open tables on the restaurant side that I could see but the hostess said they were saved for another reservation/party. One of the tables sat unused through our entire dinner. The hostesses were rude and acted put out when I requested another table and told us we’d have to wait an hour. We ultimately had to sit in the bar area. I’m honestly so disappointed with our experience. I was super excited to try this restaurant and had been looking forward to it for my birthday dinner, which makes this even more upsetting. The food was actually really good but the service completely ruined the night.

Our waiter was incredibly rude from the start. She spilled water on us and didn’t even apologize. Not once. No “I’m sorry,” no acknowledgment, nothing. It was awkward and completely unprofessional. Throughout the entire dinner, she had zero manners and treated us noticeably differently. We felt judged and dismissed the entire time.

This was supposed to be my birthday dinner. I made sure to note it in the reservation multiple times and even mentioned it again when we arrived. Not once did I get a smile, a “happy birthday,” or any acknowledgment at all. For a restaurant that presents itself as nice and upscale, the lack of basic hospitality was shocking.

We were barely checked on and did not feel taken care of. The energy was cold the entire night. The food may have been good, but the service was absolutely horrible and completely overshadowed the experience. It honestly ruined my birthday dinner.

For the prices and reputation, we expected professionalism and kindness — not to be treated poorly. Extremely disappointing.

reviews.text:
Tuve la oportunidad de celebrar mi cena de cumpleaños en Cala, y sinceramente fue una experiencia espectacular de principio a fin. Éramos un grupo de aproximadamente 10 personas y todo salió incluso mejor de lo que esperaba.
Desde antes del evento, la persona que me ayudó con la organización y la decoración superó completamente mis expectativas. Fue muy detallista, pensó en cada pequeño detalle y realmente se tomó el tiempo de hacer que todo fuera especial y personalizado. Se nota cuando alguien hace su trabajo con amor, dedicación y profesionalismo, y aquí definitivamente fue así.
Al llegar al restaurante, el ambiente era simplemente perfecto: una vibra muy bonita, tranquila, con buenas energías, ideal para conversar, compartir y disfrutar el momento. Un lugar muy ameno, acogedor y elegante a la vez.
El servicio fue impecable. La chica que nos atendió durante la cena fue súper profesional, amable y paciente, siempre con una sonrisa y dispuesta a ayudarnos en todo momento, incluso siendo un grupo grande.
La comida fue otro nivel: desde los entrantes hasta los postres, todo estuvo delicioso, bien presentado y con sabores increíbles. Se nota claramente el profesionalismo y la calidad con la que trabajan en cocina.
Sin duda, recomiendo este lugar una y mil veces más. Cala es un restaurante que cuida cada detalle, ofrece un excelente servicio y crea experiencias memorables. Para mí, se ha convertido en uno de los mejores lugares para celebrar momentos especiales.
Estoy súper agradecida y definitivamente volveré.

reviews.text:
Dinner with a DJ (no warning provided)

Arrived at Cala Scottsdale for a 6:00 PM reservation and was delighted to discover I had accidentally signed up to chaperone a college party. All I was missing was a whistle and a clipboard.

We were seated at what appeared to be portable, fold-up tables packed so tightly together that the end chairs couldn’t slide under the table. Sitting down required negotiation skills. I asked the manager if we could move to one of the larger booth tables (clearly designed for 7+ people) but was told there’s absolutely no flexibility as seating is based strictly on headcount…not comfort. A bold operational philosophy.

The space itself is sleek and upscale which suggested polished, seasoned service. Instead, the staff, including the manager, seemed very young and enthusiastic but not particularly experienced. The atmosphere promised “refined,” the service delivered “spring break.”

My bestie who invited me spent around $250 with only one alcoholic drink ordered (a single beer) which was impressive considering the food
was……fine. The meatball appetizer was the standout. The pasta was competently cooked which I assume was the goal.

Then there was the music. Club-level volume. At 6:00 PM. Conversation became a competitive sport. If the plan is to turn the restaurant into a nightlife venue, perhaps wait until after 9:00 PM once the early dinner crowd and their responsibilities have gone home.

Nothing was outright bad.  It was simply confused about what it wants to be. Restaurant? Lounge? College mixer? I’m still unclear. Either way, I won’t be returning.

My husband and I were staying at the Senna and had brunch at Cala twice, and both times were enjoyable. The French toast was especially delicious, and the champagne bottle presentation with sparklers added a festive touch as we celebrated our friends’ birthdays.

I also want to give extra praise to Cam. She mentioned she was only a few weeks into working at Cala, and when I ordered a Cala iced coffee, she wasn’t familiar with it even though I had it the day before. The drink that came out wasn’t what I expected, but that wasn’t her fault. What I really appreciated was that she came back to our table later to let us know she checked with the staff and confirmed they did have it. She asked if I wanted one, and I declined, but her effort and thoughtfulness really stood out.

We don’t know how the ambiance and food is during dinner, however it seems like it’d be a lively place.

Overall, we had a wonderful time and would definitely return if we stay in the area again or at The Senna.

reviews.text: Came for a date night dinner with friends. The restaurant is certainly beautiful and we were seated at an outside patio table with beautiful weather under the stars. With all that, we were expecting something really great and it just didn't come. I had the lemon chicken and hubby had rigatoni Bolognese. Edible, but nothing to write home about. Both of these were Italian dishes, but served with no bread. Therefore, we had to ask our server if we could have some bread and, by far, the most disappointing thing was the bread that was eventually provided. It was a very small portion, two slices of something unidentifiable, and they used some sort of strange method to toast it. It was seriously as if you asked a 5-year-old to make you some toast served in a bowl. I've honestly never seen this kind of bread service in an upscale restaurant. I know that there are great bakeries in Scottsdale that make great bread. Why this restaurant is not using those bakeries is beyond me. But if you're going to do this bread service and charge people for it, you really need to step up your game. Even the awkward flatbread served with the hummus was better!

To make things worse, a different staff member then came to our table and informed us that they couldn’t prepare the items we ordered because breakfast service had ended. This was extremely frustrating -if the kitchen couldn’t make it, we should have been told immediately when ordering, not after waiting so long.

From start to finish, our experience at CALA was nothing short of incredible—and Mason was the absolute highlight. He was attentive, on point, and truly elevated our night with the kind of service that turns a great dinner into an unforgettable experience.

The food? Outstanding. We’re still dreaming about the chicken and pasta, the tuna tartare, and that tequila espresso martini (a must-try). Every bite was perfectly executed, and the flavors spoke for themselves.

The vibes and ambiance at CALA are unmatched—warm, vibrant, and full of energy. Pair that with food this good and service as exceptional as Mason’s, and you have the recipe for a night we’ll be talking about for a long time.

We could go on and on, but simply put: thank you CALA and thank you Mason for making an already incredible establishment even more memorable. We can’t wait to come back!

I was staying at the hotel attached to this restaurant (Senna House) and decided on the morning of my flight to have breakfast at Cala. I was seated immediately & met with very attentive service.

I ordered the French Toast and my friend ordered a different dish; both were ready in ~20-30mins, not ideal but I had about 5hrs until my flight to kill. After several bites of the French toast and chit chat, I suddenly felt ill and went to the restroom. Occasionally, I’m sensitive to the amount of dairy in French toast so I suggested my friend eat the rest of it. After a few bites, she also needed the restroom. She has no dairy or other dietary restrictions so I was confused…

We left and unfortunately as a result of the meal I had at Cala, I’ve now had to postpone my flight back home and spend an extra day in the city to recover. Food poisoning is never fun, it’s inconvenient, and entirely preventable. Comping my meal (which they did), without an apology is not nearly enough for the inconvenience and cost (changing flight & booking another night at the hotel totaled to $500).

Ridiculous. Please stay away from this establishment.

reviews.text: Cala is an elegant yet inviting spot in Old Town Scottsdale, ideal for enjoying dinner or late-night bites. The Mediterranean-inspired menu features standout dishes like flaming saganaki, handmade pastas, artisan pizzas, and a standout Wagyu ribeye chop, all thoughtfully prepared with bold flavors and seasonal ingredients. Cocktails and wine pair beautifully with everything. The service is polished and engaging, offering helpful menu suggestions and keeping the pace smooth through dinner hours. And the ambiance is stellar, modern coastal design with a lush patio, warm lighting, and lively energy that feels upscale without being stuffy. Whether you're ending the evening after sunset or enjoying a late dinner, Cala delivers consistently on food, drink, and atmosphere.

reviews.text: My friend and I finally made it to Cala and it was to celebrate my birthday. I had the espresso martini and it was creamy goodness. My friend had the tasty and refreshing Plum Spritz. All the food was absolutely delicious! We had the whipped ricotta and  lamb kofta to start from the Happy Hour menu. Then we shared the  Caesar salad and Lumacha Alla Vodka. The delicious meal was finished off with a tasty key limeish dessert that was brought out with a sparkler for my birthday. I would recommend all of these items and would go back to have them all again. Our servers, Forrest and Lauren really contributed to our overall great experience. They were friendly, attentive, and accommodating. When a fly decided to enjoy the whipped ricotta with us, we said there was no need to replace it, but Forrest insisted replacing it quickly by showing up with a fresh plate of whipped ricotta. The restaurant is simple yet beautifully decorated with a calm relaxing atmosphere. I would definitely recommend Cala for the food, service, ambiance,  and overall experience.
